# Shamir Network Leakage

This repository studies information-theoretic secrecy of unchanged classical Shamir sharing against one classical leaked bit per device, assisted by independent bipartite quantum sources on arbitrary graphs. For arbitrary extensions of the independent-source device marginal, it establishes the sharp leading secrecy exponent t/2 above reconstruction rate one half by a fixed margin, and an exact even-device full-threshold optimum.

## Reading routes

- Scientific question and result table: README.md
- Connected scientific explanation and proof dependencies: science/README.md

- Input Fourier expansion, dual MDS code and output-parity identities: science/fourier.md
- Inherited graph contraction, polar trace-norm reduction and support-only second-moment bounds: science/network_bounds.md
- Full-threshold bounds, finite-prime cosine factor and matching attack: science/full_threshold.md
- General-threshold finite bounds, optimization and sharp leading exponent above one half: science/general_threshold.md
- Coherent-purification counterexample, communication and source-graph distinction: science/boundaries.md
- Primary-source comparison and precise inherited ingredients: references/RELATED_WORK.md
- Structured bibliography: references/references.bib
- Reproduction commands and interpretation: verification/README.md

- The single Watrous anchor, verified sections, notation translation and a complete Bell-pair example: learning/WATROUS_BRIDGE.md
- Exactly 30 project-defined understanding targets, dependencies and source pointers: learning/MILESTONES.md

## Distinctions to preserve

The public inputs and outputs are classical. Arbitrary local quantum processing does not mean quantum leaked outputs. The resource is independent of the secret and sharing randomness, and leakage occurs without communication or adversary feedback.

An arbitrary extension of the stated product-source device marginal includes no reference or a separate source-graph reference vertex as special cases. At full threshold with even n the exact worst-case distance over the class is 2^(1-n/2) cos(pi/(2p)). The upper bound holds graphwise and a Bell-pair matching attains it. Odd n has a matching order.

The sharp leading exponent applies at a fixed positive margin above rate one half; the security transition at and below one half remains open in this model. Explicit elementary finite bounds use q=n/(n-t+1) at least 2. An actual classical seed is treated branchwise; coherent purification of an unlabelled mixture is a different resource.

Quantum Finner, the complex contraction, Shamir Fourier methods, paired frequencies, MDS weighting and weighted list-recovery methods are inherited. The reference reduction sums the positive inactive outcomes before applying quantum Finner, and gives one weighted factor per nonzero coordinate on every independent-source graph. Use the related-work page for attribution and model comparisons.

The written proofs establish uniform claims. Finite enumerations and numerical optimizations establish only the checks described in verification/README.md.

Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), is the sole educational anchor. The bridge distinguishes the inspected author manuscript from the published book and translates its full trace-norm distance to this repository's half-trace-norm convention. The 14 background milestones end with the full leakage experiment; the 16 narrative milestones end with the scientific synthesis. Research citations support attribution and proof dependencies beyond the anchor.
